claims.text: Nearly equiatomic FeCoNiTi is a high-entropy alloy.
As-cast equiatomic FeCoNiTi contains coexisting fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves phases with chemical segregation.
Rapid quenching by arc melting on a water-cooled Cu hearth stabilizes or locks in the dual-phase FeCoNiTi microstructure.
The fcc phase has an approximate composition of Fe21.3Co24.8Ni32.2Ti21.6.
The C14 Laves phase has an approximate composition of Fe27.3Co26.6Ni17.4Ti28.7.
The fcc phase in dual-phase FeCoNiTi is ferromagnetic.
Phase boundaries and chemical segregation mediate the magnetic response of dual-phase FeCoNiTi.
Antiferromagnetic coupling between the Fe/Co/Ni and Ti sublattices in the fcc phase reduces saturation magnetization.
Antiferromagnetic sublattice coupling enhances orbital contributions in the fcc phase.
The C14 phase, together with possible spin canting, promotes domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning causes a marked increase in coercivity.
The fcc phase orders magnetically around 1084 K and has an additional transition near 168 K.
The C14 phase contributes a lower-temperature magnetic transition near 214 K.
Dual-phase FeCoNiTi should have a coercive field of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloys typically have coercivity below 100 Oe.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloys have limited orbital-moment contributions.
Multiple distinct magnetic transitions would mark the presence of both fcc and C14 phases.
The coercivity enhancement depends on coexistence and interfacial interactions between the fcc and C14 phases.
If rapid quenching fails to produce the dual-phase structure, or composition changes yield a single phase, the coercivity enhancement will not occur.

contradictions.description: Magnetic measurements are limited to temperatures up to 400 K, but the experiment proposes detecting a magnetic transition near 1084 K, which cannot be observed within that range.

The Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 comparator is described as compositionally matched to nominally equiatomic FeCoNiTi, although its Ni and Ti concentrations differ substantially from the 25 at.% values of the nominal alloy.

The initial as-cast alloy is already stated to contain the dual-phase structure, while the intervention is framed as applying rapid quenching to create or stabilize that same structure; the pre-intervention state and treatment sequence are therefore ambiguous.
